key_insight: The paper shows that unsupervised domain adaptation can make mammography calcification classifiers more reliable across hospitals and datasets without requiring labels from the target site. In simple terms, it helps AI models keep working when the imaging data comes from a new clinic with different scanner or patient distributions.
problem_solved: Breast cancer CAD models often lose accuracy when deployed on unseen multi-site mammography datasets because of domain shift. This work addresses the challenge of classifying malignant vs. benign calcifications consistently across different institutions without target-domain annotation.
method: Builds a calcification classification framework designed for cross-site mammography domain adaptation.
Uses unsupervised domain adaptation to align feature representations between source and target datasets.
Improves malignant-versus-benign prediction performance on unseen domains while avoiding the need for labeled target-site data.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this highlights a practical path toward more generalizable medical imaging models that can transfer across hospitals. It is especially valuable for deployment settings where labeling new clinical data is expensive, slow, or impractical.

paper_title: Unsupervised Domain Adaptation for Calcification Classification in Mammography Across Multi-Site Datasets
paper_authors: Xuan Liu, Derek L. Nguyen, Emily C. Barre, Jennifer Thomas, Thomas Lynch
